Messages.Body:

>Vamp has a goul retainer. 1 Shotgun 3r, and a Flamethrower 2r Ag.

>Flamethrower then burn the vamp or does the vamp luck out and go to
>torpor. It seems to me that the timing is simo but I'm not sure any

If a vampire takes a mix of aggravated and non-aggravated damage at
the same time, the non-aggro is applied first.  So the Shotgun would
hit home, then the Flamethrower, burning the vampire in this example.

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Frederic Genest <karrde@step.polymtl.ca> wrote:
>: If a vampire takes a mix of aggravated and non-aggravated damage at
>: the same time, the non-aggro is applied first.  So the Shotgun would
>: hit home, then the Flamethrower, burning the vampire in this example.
>Right, to a point.  The non-aggravated damage is applied first, but since 
>the target only has 2 BP in this example, and suffers a 3 points of 
>damage burst, it goes to torpor before the aggravated damage hits home.

You don't deal the non-aggro, pause to figure out what happened with that,
and then deal the aggro if the vampire is still around.  Bang, the non-aggro
hits, and then bang, the aggro hits and might or might not burn the vampire.
If the vampire is not burned, then it goes to torpor as appropriate.  This
is the difference between a vampire taking a mix of aggro and non-aggro in
one strike, vs. taking non-aggro in one strike and then aggro as an
additional strike.


Tom Wylie		rec.games.deckmaster Network Representative for
aahz@hal.com			Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

>damage burst, it goes to torpor before the aggravated damage hits home.
>
>Unless there is something I missed  (a Rule Group ruling for example).

Well, there was. Each strike (strike in this case being a unit of time)
has it's own damage resolution phase. If the Shotgun & FT occur as a result
of celerity. The V goes to torpor and escapes the second strike. However,
the Ghoul Retainer (and Wolf Companion, Weather Control, <sup> Drawing
Out the Beast, etc) does simultaneous damage in combination with the
striking V. Thus all damage gets resolved together.

Thus V burns.

Messages.Author: Doug  Dejulio
Messages.Body:
In article <3a9smt$7be@perv.hal.com>, Tom Wylie <aahz@hal.COM> wrote:
>Trevor Barrie <tbarrie@bud.peinet.pe.ca> wrote:
>>If the non-aggravated damage is enough to send the vampire into torport, would
>>a single point of aggravated damage be sufficient to burn the vampire? Or 
>>would it require two aggro to burn, as with any other zero-blood vampire?
>
>It always requires at least two aggravated damage to burn a vampire outright.

This makes no sense.

The reason it normally takes two aggrivated damage to burn a vampire
outright is that the first simply sends the vampire to torpor.  Any
vampire in torpor who takes aggrivated damage is burned, so the 2nd
point burns them.

So, if you've got a vampire who has one blood, who takes nine points
of normal damage and 1 aggrivated at the same time, the recent ruling
that you apply the non-aggrivated damage first *should* mean the
vampire burns.

-- 
Doug DeJulio
ddj+@pitt.edu

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
->  If a vampire takes a mix of aggravated and non-aggravated damage,
the non-aggravated is applied first, to maximize the chances of burning
the vampire outright.

->  "...  thus the vampire loses no blood, unless more than one aggravated
damage is received.  In this case the excess is paid in blood...  If the
vampire does not have the blood to heal excess aggravated damage, then it
is considered destroyed and its card is burned."  (page 32)  So the first
point of aggravated damage always sends the vampire to torpor rather than
actually damaging it; whether it had already taken enough non-aggravated
to torpor it is irrelevant.  Only if more than one aggravated damage is dealt,
and that excess cannot be healed, is the vampire burned outright.


Tom Wylie		rec.games.deckmaster Network Representative for
aahz@hal.com			Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Messages.Author: Christopher Clark
Messages.Body:
->  "...  thus the vampire loses no blood, unless more than one aggravated
   damage is received.  In this case the excess is paid in blood...  If the
   vampire does not have the blood to heal excess aggravated damage, then it
   is considered destroyed and its card is burned."  (page 32)  So the first
   point of aggravated damage always sends the vampire to torpor rather than
   actually damaging it; whether it had already taken enough non-aggravated
   to torpor it is irrelevant.  Only if more than one aggravated damage is
   dealt, and that excess cannot be healed, is the vampire burned outright.

  Which, IMHO, is stupid.  We've always played it so that if the vampire was
in torpor when they took aggravated damage, it was treated like the first
point had already occured, because that made sense to us.

  -- Chris Clark

Messages.Author: Eric Masson
Messages.Body:
Hello,

I play MtG about once every week with a few of friends who have much
more time and money than I do to invest in the game. Initially I was
capable of holding my end but they've caught on to my tricks and
tactics in addition to purchasing so many individual
cards at high prices that I can't follow anymore. And there is no
way I'll dish out a few more hundred bucks to keep up with them. 

The game is getting excessively boring and predictable. It's getting
to be a trivial combinatorics problem to play the game. And, with at most
seven cards in hand at any time, I find there is little
challenge in finding the right card to play.  It's automatic.
My only chances occur in multi-player matches where I manage to play
my opponents against each other. 

I'm desperately trying to revive an interest in the game. Does anyone
know of decks made of high frequency cards which will hold
their own against loaded decks ? Despite my many cards I have
no Counterspell and Sera Angel cards. We play with at most 
4 cards of any type but mana and at most 1 artifact of each kind. 
My opponents play darks and some legends in addition to revised cards. I
only have revised cards. Decks of any color subset will do as I am grateful
for any reply. I'm even willing to purchase a few low end uncommon cards
to help my cause 8) I look forward to your responses.

Thanks to anyone who'll manage to show me that Magic isn't a war
of the wallets and that there is indeed a profound art in deck
building.

Eric

Two word answer: Pestilence Deck!!
A nice little idea I came up with, it requires primarily common cards, 
and works well with almost entirely revised!

Here is the basic concept: the deck is white/black, you try to get out
a circle of protection black, a pestilence, a regenerating creature
and you are in business!  Just keep pestilencing, using your circle to
protect yourself and remember to regenerate your creature!

A good base for the deck is:
4 CoP: Black
2 CoP: Red (so you can't be fireballed to death!!)
4 Pestilence
4 Drudge Skeletons
4 Walking dead (a common Legends card, identical to drugde skeletons)
4 Dark Rituals
some walls of swords (lots of health, good to stop flyers)
4 disenchants (to stop you opponents from using CoP Black :)
a couple of regenerating walls
as many will'o'the wisps as you can gather
a Sacrifice or two
a Demo-tutor or two if you have any
a bunch of swamps and plains

Keep in mind not to bring out TOO many creatures at once,otherwise you
won't have enough mana to regerate them all!!
Good luck!
Warning: in multiplayer games, everyone will find you VERY aggravating,
and will probably gang up and kill you :(


	Dave Woods
	dwoods@io.org

Beating any single deck is an almost mindless proposition.  Simply change your  strategy, colors, or focus.  This leaves a player expecting to play a certain
deck with a LOT of useless cards in his or her hand.  Think about it:  A person with black hosers, COP black, karma, lifeforce, etc, will find nothing to do
with them against any color BUT black.  Same for any hoser.  Then, don't allow
deck tuning unless the overcarded fool changes to an entirely different deck.

Honest, the most wildly successful deck I've ever seen was comprised entirely of common cards and Arabian Nights commons (ok, this was a year ago, when arabians were still common.)

Three words:  Speed, Speed, Speed.
When trading, know what you want, and what you're willing to give for them.  I
know one person who has spent $150 total, and is one of the best players I've
ever played.  He has 3 GOOD decks.

What follows is a fairly flexible low-cost deck that has proved consistently 
  competent against high-cost decks.  It's one of the four "test decks" guys
  here uses to test our tournament decks.  All cards are common in Revised
  unless otherwise noted.  This deck is constructed to be tournament-legal.
  We dismantle our tournament decks if they can't beat this (and the other
  three test decks) on a consistent basis.

Main Deck:

  Black Vise (Revised uncommon)
  Brassclaw Orcs (x2) (Fallen Empires common)
  Chain Lightning (x4) (Legends common)
  Channel (Revised uncommon)
  Disintegrate (x4)
  Fireball (x4)
  Forest (x9)
  Grizzly Bears (x3)
  Hurrican (x2) (Revised uncommon)
  Kird Ape (x4)
  Llanowar Elves (x4)
  Lightning Bolt (x4)
  Mountain (x10)
  Regrowth (Revised uncommon)
  Tranquility (x3)
  Shatterstorm (x2) (Revised uncommon)
  Sol Ring (Revised uncommon)
  Stone Rain

Revised common:        45 
Revised uncommon:       8
Legends common:         4
Fallen Empires common:  3
Total:                 60

Sideboard:

  Brassclaw Orcs (Fallen Empires common)
  Desert Twister (Revised uncommon)
  Flashfires (Revised uncommon)
  Grizzly Bears
  Lifeforce (x2) (Revised uncommon)
  Red Elemental Blast (x4)
  Shatterstorm (Revised uncommon)
  Stone Rain (x3)
  Tranquility

Revised common:         9
Revised uncommon:       5
Fallen Empires common:  1
Total:                 15


Some of the more expensive cards that you want to sub in for cards in 
  the basic deck if you get your hands on them:

  Library of Alexandria
  Mishra's Factory (x4)
  Sylvan Library
  Whirling Dervishes (x4)

How to play this deck? Hammer your opponent with two creatures (hold the rest
  in your hand).  Save your direct damage spells for your opponent's blockers.
  Only use the direct damage spells on your opponent to finish him off, do
  NOT cast direct damage spells on your opponent just because you can.  And
  remember to use your sideboard and the Channel-Fireball-Red Elemental Blast
  combo.

Hope that helps.
